title: Angles and Polygons
description: Angle facts for straight lines, parallel lines, triangles and quadrilaterals, plus interior and exterior angle sums of polygons.

notes.heading: Angle Facts on a Line and at a Point
notes.body:
📌 Definition
We measure angles in degrees ($^\circ$). Three basic angle facts come from straight lines and points.

🔑 Key Concept
• Angles on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$.
• Angles at a point add up to $360^\circ$.
• Vertically opposite angles (formed where two straight lines cross) are equal.

💡 Worked Example 1 — angles on a line
Two angles lie on a straight line and one of them is $63^\circ$. Find the other.

$$180^\circ - 63^\circ = 117^\circ$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — angles at a point
Three angles at a point are $95^\circ$, $130^\circ$ and $x$. Their total must be $360^\circ$:

$$x = 360^\circ - 95^\circ - 130^\circ = 135^\circ$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Reaching for $90^\circ$ because a line "looks upright". A straight-line angle is $180^\circ$; $90^\circ$ is only for right angles.

✅ Check
Two angles on a line are $4x$ and $x$: $5x = 180$, so $x = 36$ and the angles are $144^\circ$ and $36^\circ$.

notes.heading: Parallel Lines: F, Z and U Angles
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A transversal is a line that cuts across two (or more) other lines. When the two lines are parallel, three pairs of angles have fixed relationships.

🔑 Key Concept
For parallel lines cut by a transversal:
• Corresponding angles ("F" angles) are equal.
• Alternate angles ("Z" angles) are equal.
• Co-interior angles ("U" or "C" angles) add up to $180^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example 1
Line $a$ is parallel to line $b$, and one of the angles at the transversal is $70^\circ$. Then every angle in the diagram is either $70^\circ$ or $110^\circ$: its corresponding and alternate partners are $70^\circ$, and its co-interior partner is $180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — solving with parallel-line angles
Two co-interior angles are $x$ and $3x - 20^\circ$. Find $x$.

$$x + 3x - 20^\circ = 180^\circ \implies 4x = 200^\circ \implies x = 50^\circ$$

The two angles are $50^\circ$ and $130^\circ$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using these facts when the lines are NOT parallel. Only use F/Z/U facts when the diagram shows the parallel arrows on both lines.

✅ Tip
Trace the shape of the letter with your pencil: the "F" hides corresponding angles, the "Z" hides alternate angles, the "U" hides co-interior angles.

notes.heading: Angles in Triangles
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The three interior angles of any triangle add up to $180^\circ$.

🔑 Key Concept
• Triangle angle sum: $180^\circ$.
• Isosceles triangle: the two base angles (opposite the equal sides) are equal.
• Equilateral triangle: all angles are $60^\circ$.
• Exterior angle of a triangle = sum of the two interior angles NOT adjacent to it.

💡 Worked Example 1
Two angles of a triangle are $40^\circ$ and $65^\circ$. The third is $180^\circ - 40^\circ - 65^\circ = 75^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — isosceles
An isosceles triangle has a top (apex) angle of $40^\circ$. The two base angles are equal, so each is

$$\frac{180^\circ - 40^\circ}{2} = 70^\circ$$

💡 Worked Example 3 — exterior angle
The two angles remote from an exterior angle are $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$, so the exterior angle is $110^\circ$. (Check: the interior angle next to it is $70^\circ$, and $110^\circ + 70^\circ = 180^\circ$ on a straight line.)

⚠️ Common Misconception
Assuming a triangle is isosceles because two angles "look similar". Use only the tick marks on the sides, or worked-out values.

✅ Check
A triangle has angles $x$, $2x$ and $2x$: $5x = 180$, so $x = 36$ and the angles are $36^\circ$, $72^\circ$, $72^\circ$.

notes.heading: Angles in Quadrilaterals
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A quadrilateral is any four-sided shape. Its four interior angles add up to $360^\circ$.

🔑 How it works
One diagonal splits any quadrilateral into two triangles, and $180^\circ + 180^\circ = 360^\circ$.
For special quadrilaterals: in a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles add up to $180^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example 1
Three angles of a quadrilateral are $85^\circ$, $110^\circ$ and $95^\circ$. The fourth angle is

$$360^\circ - 85^\circ - 110^\circ - 95^\circ = 70^\circ$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — parallelogram
One angle of a parallelogram is $60^\circ$. The opposite angle is also $60^\circ$, and each adjacent angle is $180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Mixing up the totals: triangles use $180^\circ$, quadrilaterals use $360^\circ$. A four-sided shape never has an angle sum of $180^\circ$.

✅ Check
A kite has angles $80^\circ$, $80^\circ$ and $40^\circ$; the fourth is $360^\circ - 200^\circ = 160^\circ$.

notes.heading: Interior Angle Sums of Polygons
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A polygon with $n$ sides can be split into $(n-2)$ triangles by drawing all diagonals from one vertex.

🔑 Key Formula
The sum of the interior angles of an $n$-sided polygon is

$$S = (n-2) \times 180^\circ$$

💡 Worked Example 1 — finding the sum
Pentagon: $(5-2) \times 180^\circ = 540^\circ$. Hexagon: $(6-2) \times 180^\circ = 720^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — finding the number of sides
A polygon has interior angle sum $1260^\circ$. Then $n - 2 = 1260 \div 180 = 7$, so the polygon has $9$ sides.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Triangle $180^\circ$, quadrilateral $360^\circ$, pentagon $540^\circ$, hexagon $720^\circ$ — worth memorising.
• The sum always increases by $180^\circ$ per extra side.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Writing $n-1$ instead of $n-2$ triangles. Test the formula on a triangle: $(3-2) \times 180^\circ = 180^\circ$ — it must work.

notes.heading: Exterior Angles and Regular Polygons
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An exterior angle is the turn at one vertex as you walk once around the polygon. At any vertex, interior + exterior $= 180^\circ$ (they lie on a straight line).

🔑 Key Concept
• The exterior angles of ANY convex polygon add up to $360^\circ$.
• For a regular polygon with $n$ sides: exterior angle $= 360^\circ \div n$ and interior angle $= 180^\circ - \frac{360^\circ}{n}$.

💡 Worked Example 1 — regular octagon
Exterior angle: $360^\circ \div 8 = 45^\circ$. Interior angle: $180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — working backwards
A regular polygon has interior angles of $150^\circ$. Each exterior angle is $180^\circ - 150^\circ = 30^\circ$, so

$$n = \frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ} = 12$$

The polygon is a regular dodecagon (12 sides).

✅ Check
Regular nonagon: exterior $40^\circ$, interior $140^\circ$ — and $(9-2) \times 180^\circ = 1260^\circ = 9 \times 140^\circ$. ✓

notes.heading: Angle Reasoning in Compound Diagrams
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A compound diagram mixes several shapes. The marks (ticks for equal sides, arrows for parallel lines, squares for right angles) tell you which facts are allowed.

🔑 How to work through one
1. Mark every angle you can already name.
2. Look for isosceles triangles, straight lines and parallel lines.
3. Step from angle to angle, giving a reason at each step ("angle sum of a triangle", "alternate angles, AB ∥ CD", ...).

💡 Worked Example 1 — square with an equilateral triangle
An equilateral triangle is drawn inside a square on one of its sides. At a shared corner, the angle between a triangle side and the square side is $90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — ratio angles
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2 : 3 : 4$. The $9$ equal parts add to $180^\circ$, so one part is $20^\circ$ and the angles are $40^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $80^\circ$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Never claim two angles are equal "because they look the same size". Diagrams are NOT drawn to scale in IGCSE unless the question says so — every statement needs a geometry reason.

✅ Tip
If a question says "Give reasons for your answer", write the name of the angle fact next to each step — that is where the method marks are.

flashcards.definition: Equal — formed where two straight lines cross.
flashcards.example: If one pair is $70^\circ$, the opposite angle is also $70^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: Equal when a transversal cuts parallel lines.
flashcards.example: A $70^\circ$ angle at line $a$ matches $70^\circ$ at line $b$.

flashcards.definition: Equal when a transversal cuts parallel lines.
flashcards.example: A $70^\circ$ angle on one side of the transversal pairs with $70^\circ$ on the other.

flashcards.definition: Add up to $180^\circ$ when lines are parallel.
The three interior angles add to $180^\circ$.
The angles opposite the two equal sides are equal.
flashcards.example: Apex $40^\circ$ gives base angles of $70^\circ$ each.

flashcards.definition: Equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
The four interior angles add to $360^\circ$.
Always add to $360^\circ$; a regular $n$-gon has exterior angle $360^\circ \div n$.

questions.stem: Two angles lie on a straight line. One of them is $63^\circ$. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$, so the other angle is $180^\circ - 63^\circ = 117^\circ$.

questions.stem: Three of the angles at a point are $90^\circ$, $120^\circ$ and $100^\circ$. What is the fourth?
questions.explanation: Angles at a point add up to $360^\circ$. The three given angles total $310^\circ$, so the fourth is $360^\circ - 310^\circ = 50^\circ$.

questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle are $55^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$: $180^\circ - 55^\circ - 60^\circ = 65^\circ$.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.explanation: A hexagon has $n = 6$ sides, so the interior angle sum is $(6-2) \times 180^\circ = 720^\circ$.

questions.stem: What is the size of each exterior angle of a regular decagon (10 sides)?
questions.explanation: The exterior angles of any polygon total $360^\circ$. For a regular decagon each exterior angle is $360^\circ \div 10 = 36^\circ$.

questions.stem: Line $a$ is parallel to line $b$. A transversal makes an angle of $74^\circ$ with line $a$. What is the co-interior (U) angle with it at line $b$?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to $180^\circ$: $180^\circ - 74^\circ = 106^\circ$.

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of $48^\circ$. What is the size of each base angle?
questions.explanation: The base angles are equal and all three angles total $180^\circ$, so each base angle is $(180^\circ - 48^\circ) \div 2 = 66^\circ$.

questions.stem: Three angles of a quadrilateral are $88^\circ$, $97^\circ$ and $121^\circ$. Find the fourth angle.
questions.explanation: Quadrilateral angles total $360^\circ$. The three given angles sum to $306^\circ$, so the fourth is $360^\circ - 306^\circ = 54^\circ$.

questions.stem: A polygon has interior angles that add up to $900^\circ$. How many sides does it have?
A triangle has an exterior angle. The two interior angles remote from it are $45^\circ$ and $70^\circ$. What is the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $45^\circ + 70^\circ = 115^\circ$.

questions.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is $144^\circ$. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle is $180^\circ - 144^\circ = 36^\circ$, and the number of sides is $360^\circ \div 36^\circ = 10$.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2 : 3 : 4$. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: The ratio has $2+3+4 = 9$ equal parts totalling $180^\circ$, so one part is $20^\circ$ and the largest angle is $4 \times 20^\circ = 80^\circ$.

questions.stem: $AB$ is parallel to $CD$. Point $P$ lies between the two lines so that angle $ABP = 35^\circ$ and angle $DCP = 42^\circ$. What is angle $BPC$?
questions.explanation: Draw a line through $P$ parallel to $AB$ and $CD$. The new line splits angle $BPC$ into two alternate angles of $35^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, so angle $BPC = 35^\circ + 42^\circ = 77^\circ$.

questions.stem: A regular pentagon and an equilateral triangle share one full side. At an endpoint of that side, what is the angle between a side of the triangle and a side of the pentagon?
questions.explanation: Each interior angle of a regular pentagon is $108^\circ$ and each angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^\circ$. The angle between them is $108^\circ - 60^\circ = 48^\circ$.

questions.stem: The four angles of a quadrilateral are $x$, $2x$, $3x$ and $4x$. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: Quadrilateral angles total $360^\circ$: $x + 2x + 3x + 4x = 10x = 360^\circ$, so $x = 36^\circ$ and the largest angle is $4x = 144^\circ$.
